nodes.name: Aza-CMP synthesis
nodes.procedure: 532.5 mg (1.875 mmol) of 1,2,4,5-benzenetetraamine tetrahydrochloride in 15 ml of anhydrous DMF and 390 mg (1.25 mmol) of hexaketocyclohexane octahydrate in 5 ml of anhydrous DMF were mixed and refluxed for 48 h under argon. The dark brown solid was purified via hot extraction with methanol for 48 h using a Soxhlet extractor. The resulting solid was dried under vacuum at 150 °C for 24 h.

nodes.source_text: Aza-CMP was prepared according to a literature-reported route27. Here 532.5 mg (1.875 mmol) of 1,2,4,5-benzenetetramine tetrahydrochloride in 15 ml of anhydrous DMF and 390 mg (1.25 mmol) of hexaketocyclohexane octahydrate in 5 ml of anhydrous DMF were mixed and refluxed for 48 h under argon.

nodes.name: Aza-CMP–Ni complexation
nodes.procedure: 20 mg of Aza-CMP was immersed in 10 ml of anhydrous DMF, and the suspension was ultrasonically dispersed and kept stirring for 30 min with argon bubbling through the solution. Then, 84 mg (1.5 eq. with respect to phenanthroline units) of nickel(II) acetate tetrahydrate was dissolved in 10 ml of anhydrous DMF under an argon atmosphere. Ni²⁺ solution was slowly added to the suspension under the argon atmosphere, and the mixture was kept dispersed by ultrasonication for 8 h at room temperature. The solid was filtered using a polytetrafluoroethylene membrane and then washed with DMF, water, methanol and ethanol sequentially until the filtrate became colourless. Finally, the product was dried at 60 °C under vacuum conditions overnight.

nodes.name: Fe-saturated NaOH preparation
nodes.procedure: 1 mg of FeCl3 was mixed with 10 ml of 1.0 M NaOH in a 50-ml propylene centrifuge tube. The yellow suspension was agitated and filtered with a 0.2-μm syringe filter. The obtained colourless filtrate was noted as an Fe-saturated NaOH solution.

nodes.name: Aza-CMP–NiFe electrochemical formation
nodes.procedure: Aza-CMP–Ni was first deposited onto the CP electrode by the drop-casting method. The obtained Aza-CMP–Ni/CP electrode was used as a working electrode in a standard three-electrode cell. CV of Aza-CMP–Ni/CP was conducted in Fe-saturated NaOH at a scanning window of 0.25–0.75 V versus Hg–HgO using common glassware as the electrochemical cell. The gradual formation of Ni–Fe sites is accompanied by a noticeable increase in OER current and the significant evolution of gas bubbles. After the current reached the steady state, the electrocatalyst on the CP was denoted as Aza-CMP–NiFe.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni centres in Aza-CMP–Ni show oxidation states of +2.2 at OCP and 1.2 V, +2.6 at 1.5 V, and +3.2 at 1.8 V versus RHE, indicating stepwise oxidation from Ni²⁺ to Ni³⁺ to Ni⁴⁺.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni centres in Aza-CMP–Ni show an oxidation state of +2.2 at open circuit potential (OCP) and 1.2 V versus RHE. At a potential of 1.5 V, the Ni oxidation state reaches +2.6 ... At 1.8 V, the Ni oxidation state increases to +3.2, indicating the presence of Ni⁴⁺ states.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni centres in Aza-CMP–NiFe show oxidation state of +2.1 at OCP and 1.2 V versus RHE, reaching only +2.5 under 1.7 V, implying absence of Ni⁴⁺ during catalysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni centres in Ni–Fe sites show oxidation state of +2.1 at OCP and 1.2 V versus RHE ... the Ni oxidation state only reaches +2.5 under 1.7 V, implying the absence of Ni⁴⁺ during catalysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES shows Fe oxidation states of +3.1 at 1.2 V and +3.4 at 1.7 V versus RHE in Aza-CMP–NiFe, with nonlinear model giving +3.3 and +4.0, confirming Fe⁴⁺ formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe oxidation states are +3.1 at 1.2 V and +3.4 at 1.7 V ... When using a nonlinear model with references from +2 to +6, these values increase to +3.3 and +4.0.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy of Aza-CMP–NiFe shows 69% of Fe³⁺ sites further oxidized to Fe⁴⁺ after Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ redox transition at 1.38 V versus RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2g shows a comparison of spectra collected at 1.10 V and 1.38 V versus RHE, revealing a distinct feature signal emerging after the Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ redox transition. This signal is characteristic of Fe⁴⁺ species, with 69% of Fe³⁺ sites further oxidized.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni and Fe concentrations in Aza-CMP–Ni and Aza-CMP–NiFe determined using multiple wavelengths; loading calculated as 1.8×10⁻⁸ mol cm⁻² for redox-active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The metal concentration was calculated using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy ... Ni concentrations were determined using three different wavelengths: 216.5 nm, 230.3 nm and 361.9 nm; Fe concentrations were determined using three different wavelengths: 238.2 nm, 273.0 nm and 371.9 nm. The average concentrations obtained at different wavelengths were taken for data evaluation.
